status.text: The London office at 1 Water Lane is on the founder page. Care Talk reported on 15 April 2026 that Cera was launching an AI lab, and the BBC profile of 1 October 2026 still names Ben Maruthappu as founder and chief executive.

traction.text: Dr Ben Maruthappu co-founded Cera in 2016. He is a doctor, previously advised the chief executive of NHS England, and was educated at Oxford, Cambridge, and Harvard. TechCrunch reported on 12 January 2025 that Cera raised 150 million dollars, mostly debt, and had raised more than 407 million dollars in total. The BBC wrote on 1 October 2026 that Cera says it has 13,500 staff and almost 500 million pounds of annual revenue.

who_pays.text: Governments, insurers, and the NHS pay, the mission page says. No public price. A family price was not on the mission page or in the January 2025 TechCrunch report. No reimbursement tariff for a private buyer was found.

what_it_does.text: Cera sends carers and nurses to homes in the UK. Its mission page says the work is for governments, insurers, and the NHS, and that carers log visits so the company can flag risks. TechCrunch reported the notes are used to predict falls and hospital stays.

why_interesting.text: Cera employs the carers, so the warning claims rest on its own visit notes. The BBC figures and the hospital percentages are the company's, and the January 2025 money was mostly debt.

title: Confidant
research_summary: an app for parental control and care of the elderly.
job: Confidant is a phone app from Confidant Technologies in Valencia. A family member can see where an older person's Android phone or watch is, get an alert when they leave or arrive at set places, and start a video call that opens on the other device so they can see and hear what is happening. The same app can lock apps and is also sold for watching children. The older person can wear a watch and does not have to tap the screen.
who_pays: Families pay. In November 2023, founder Jose Rogero told the EFE news agency that one device cost €9.99 a month and five devices cost €19.99 a month, with a free version for basic safety. The live website does not list a price, so those figures may have changed.

what_it_does.text: Confidant is a phone app from Confidant Technologies in Valencia. A family member can see where an older person's Android phone or watch is, get an alert when they leave or arrive at set places, and start a video call that opens on the other device so they can see and hear what is happening. The same app can lock apps and is also sold for watching children. The older person can wear a watch and does not have to tap the screen.

who_pays.text: Families pay. In November 2023, founder Jose Rogero told the EFE news agency that one device cost €9.99 a month and five devices cost €19.99 a month, with a free version for basic safety. The live website does not list a price, so those figures may have changed.

traction.text: EFE reported in November 2023 that the app had thousands of users, mainly in Spain, and also in Mexico and Switzerland. The first paid version launched at Christmas 2018 through the Lanzadera accelerator in Valencia. Google Play still lists the app under Confidant Technologies S.L. in Valencia, last updated on 3 March 2025.

why_interesting.text: Rogero built it after his mother-in-law, who later developed Alzheimer's, stopped answering the phone and the family had to drive over to check she was safe. The check is a video call that opens by itself, and the app can also stop the phone being switched off or put into flight mode. That is a different bargain from a button alarm: the family can look in, and the older person does not have to do anything.

status.text: The website is live and Google Play still distributes the app, with an update dated 3 March 2025. In November 2023 the founder said dedicated phones and a watch, with fall detection, were planned for early 2024. No later page confirmed that those devices went on sale.
